subject.title: [security] Pending OAuth login buckets collapse behind unconfigured Node reverse proxies

question: What OAuth admission policy should Node use when login traffic arrives through a peer that is not configured in `CRABBOX_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`?
rationale: The repository must choose between an upgrade-sensitive fail-closed setup error and a more complex aggregation-safe anonymous limiter; source evidence cannot determine the intended security-versus-availability policy.

options.title: Fail closed with diagnostics
options.body: Reject OAuth starts carrying proxy evidence from an untrusted peer and provide precise startup, doctor, and runtime remediation for configuring trusted CIDRs.

options.title: Add aggregation-safe limiting
options.body: Keep login available behind an untrusted shared peer but introduce non-IP admission control and focused abuse backoff that preserves downstream fairness.

options.title: Retain operator-only mitigation
options.body: Keep the current limiter and documentation contract, accepting the bounded login denial of service when reverse-proxy trust is unconfigured.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with diagnostics
recommendation.body: Reject OAuth starts carrying proxy evidence from an untrusted peer and provide precise startup, doctor, and runtime remediation for configuring trusted CIDRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged OAuth hardening established the current admission contract and its test coverage, making them the strongest history-based decision owner.
